title: StratusAI discovery - migration OpenAI -> Dedicated
summary: Initial discovery to evaluate migrating from OpenAI hosted to Redwood Dedicated. Covered current volume, cost/latency pain points, compatibility questions (OpenAI API parity), vLLM/TGI concerns for on-prem, SOC2/KMS requirements, and proposed pilot/bench plan.
next_steps: Send Dedicated pricing and 3-month pilot proposal
Share SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and network diagram
Run perf benchmark using Stratus sample prompts (Redwood SE to provision)
Schedule technical deep dive with Stratus infra team week of Jul 27
action_items: Jesse Park - Send Dedicated pricing + pilot proposal - Due: 2026-07-23
Lina Gomez - Prep benchmark plan and ask for sample prompt set + representative payloads - Due: 2026-07-22
Aisha Khan - Share sample prompts and traffic profile (QPS, avg token lengths) - Due: 2026-07-23
Maya Li - Confirm network/VPC constraints and KMS preferences - Due: 2026-07-24
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Park (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Stratus CTO), Dev Patel (ML Eng), Maya Li (Infra)

[00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jesse Park, AE on the Redwood team, with Lina Gomez who is our Solutions Engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha: Hi Jesse, thanks. Doing good, bit of a crazy week but excited to chat.
[00:12] Dev: Hey all.
[00:14] Maya: Hi.
[00:16] Lina: Great, thanks for the time. Quick agenda — we wanted to understand your current stack, what isn't working, and talk through migration paths to Dedicated or Private, plus next steps for a pilot. Sound OK?
[00:28] Aisha: Yep, that sounds right. High level: we started on OpenAI hosted about a year ago for our customer support agent product. It's easy and fast but costs are creeping and latency spikes as we scale. We're evaluating Dedicated providers and on-prem options.
[00:44] Jesse: Got it. Can you give us some rough numbers — QPS, tokens per request, percent streaming vs batch, current model family?
[00:53] Dev: Sure. Right now we're doing around 4-6 qps average during peak, 500-700 requests per minute. Typical prompt + response is about 350 tokens. We use GPT-4-like models for policy evals and gpt-3.5-ish for smaller tasks. Mostly non-streaming but we have a streaming path. Latency target is sub-400ms tail for most user-visible flows.
[01:15] Lina: Thanks. Are you seeing specific cost pain versus latency? Like are you OK paying more for lower tail latency?
[01:23] Aisha: The business cares about latency — it affects user retention — but there's a hard cost ceiling. We're trying to reduce per-token spend and also avoid tail latency spikes during bursts. OpenAI has been fine functional-wise but unpredictable at 95th/99th.
[01:36] Jesse: Makes sense. Two common levers are moving to Dedicated (predictable throughput) and tuning batching/caching/quantization — Redwood Optimize can suggest settings. Any enterprise security constraints we should know about?
[01:50] Maya: Yes — SOC2 is mandatory, we need KMS-backed key management for customer data, SSO via SAML, and audit logs per route. Also need clarity on data residency — EU region for a significant portion of our users.
[02:05] Lina: We support SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations; audit logs per request are available in the Console. For Dedicated we can deploy in an EU region and integrate with customer KMS. We'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 report after this call.
[02:20] Aisha: Great. One blocker we keep running into is API compatibility. We built a layer that relies on OpenAI semantics and we're worried about eval parity — e.g., same outputs for our prompt sets and same stop behavior. How close is Redwood to OpenAI API semantics?
[02:36] Lina: Good question. Redwood Hosted provides API parity shims for common OpenAI endpoints, but parity depends on the underlying model. For Dedicated, if you run a model that's functionally equivalent to your OpenAI model (same weights), we can configure runtime to match tokenization, sampling defaults, and streaming chunks. There are often small diffs — people do eval parity runs.
[02:56] Dev: Are there known differences with things like logprobs, stop sequences, or temperature defaults when you move from OpenAI to a locally hosted model like a vLLM/TGI stack?
[03:06] Lina: Yes, behavior can differ. vLLM/TGI stacks expose lower-level controls and sometimes different tokenization. We recommend doing eval parity tests against your prompt suite. Redwood can run head-to-head benchmarks to capture metric deltas (ROUGE, exact match, business-specific metrics).
[03:22] Jesse: To add — we often see customers take two paths: 1) keep hosted API and use Redwood Hosted as a drop-in (fastest), or 2) move to Redwood Dedicated where you get reserved GPU pools and the same control plane. For on-prem/private, you may run TGI/vLLM under our private deployment but expectation is you'll need extra validation for parity.
[03:42] Aisha: We're leaning Dedicated first. We want predictable throughput and the legal team prefers not to have all data go through public endpoints. But Dev is worried about model parity — we have a number of sensitive prompts where small wording changes are a big deal.
[03:56] Dev: Exactly. For compliance and for downstream models, we need deterministic outputs within a small margin. Also inference speed — some of the vLLM stacks are faster for certain sequence lengths, but our ops folks say they don't want to manage kernels.
[04:11] Maya: Ops wants this to be low-touch — ideally Redwood handles runtime, kernel selection, autoscaling, and we manage only the network/VPC and keys.
[04:20] Lina: That's a common ask. Dedicated provides that: we manage the serving runtime and orchestration; you get reserved capacity. For kernel & compilation choices, our runtime auto-selects kernels based on model type and sequence length; we can also lock policies if you want determinism.
[04:36] Aisha: What's the typical timeline for a Dedicated migration? From contract to running traffic?
[04:42] Jesse: For a standard Dedicated reservation with Redwood-managed hardware, it's often 4-8 weeks depending on region and onboarding needs. Private on-prem can take longer. For pilot/proof-of-concept we can provision a smaller pool in 1-2 weeks to run benchmarks.
[04:55] Dev: OK. For the benchmark, we want to run our 2k-sample prompt set, measure p50/p95/p99, token cost, and quality metrics. Can Redwood run that in your environment against the same model family?
[05:07] Lina: Yes. We'll need your sample prompts and a representative traffic profile. We can run head-to-head: your current OpenAI baseline vs Dedicated instance vs an on-prem vLLM variant if you want to test. We'll provide a benchmark report with latency percentiles, token/unit economics, and eval metrics.
[05:22] Aisha: That sounds perfect. Another question: what about streaming? Our front-end relies on 200-300ms first token in many flows. Is Redwood's streaming implementation compatible?
[05:32] Lina: We support streaming and function calling. Streaming performance depends on the runtime and network topology — for Dedicated with regional colocated infra we regularly meet sub-200ms first-byte p50 on typical models, p95 depends on sequence lengths. We'll include streaming latencies in the benchmark.
[05:49] Dev: Any gotchas with stop sequences or function-calling when switching runtime? We've seen slight hiccups where the SDK or newline tokenization changes behavior.
[05:58] Lina: Yep, tokenization differences can cause subtle stop-sequence issues. Part of parity testing is to capture those. We can also expose tokenizer configuration and ensure you're running the exact byte-pair encoding as baseline. If necessary, we can patch in tokenizer mapping or run the same model binary.
[06:15] Maya: Security again — for Dedicated, do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM and can you provide per-request audit logs exported to our SIEM?
[06:24] Jesse: Yes — Dedicated supports customer KMS and audit log export; we can stream logs to your S3 or SIEM via secure forwarders. We'll detail the integrations in the security packet.
[06:34] Aisha: On price — do you have example unit economics for our volume? We're currently at about 20M tokens/day across all flows, expecting to double in 6 months.
[06:44] Jesse: We'll put together a tailored pricing and cost model in the follow-up. Typical Dedicated economics show ~30-50% per-token reduction depending on batching and cache hit rate versus hosted. But we'll model your specific prompt mix and traffic.
[06:57] Dev: What about model updates — if we need to upgrade to a newer model family, how are rollouts handled? Canary? A/B?
[07:05] Lina: Our Console supports canary rollouts, traffic splits, and automatic fallbacks to previous model variants. That works across Hosted and Dedicated. For Private, we support the same control plane if network allows.
[07:16] Aisha: OK great. I think the next step is the benchmark. We'll share the prompt set and traffic numbers. Can we do the technical deep dive with Lina and Maya next week?
[07:26] Jesse: Absolutely — Lina, are you available week of Jul 27 for a deeper infra session?
[07:30] Lina: Yes, let's book it. I'll send a calendar invite and prep a test plan.
[07:34] Maya: Works for me.
[07:36] Aisha: Thanks, everyone.
[07:37] Jesse: Cool — recap of next steps: we'll send Dedicated pricing + pilot proposal, Lina will prep benchmark plan, Stratus will share prompts and traffic profile, Maya will confirm KMS/VPC constraints. We'll follow up with security docs.
[07:51] Aisha: Perfect. Thanks again.

Notes / nuggets:
- Customer clearly motivated by predictable throughput and cost savings; security constraints favor Dedicated over Hosted.
- Main technical risk: eval parity & tokenization differences if switching model runtime (vLLM/TGI). Customer wants head-to-head benchmark.
- Redwood can provision small Dedicated pilot in 1-2 weeks and run the 2k prompt suite.
- Action items assigned and dates agreed.

End of transcript.
